decisions.statement: A top-level statement that declares nothing runs as its body loads.
Every name a statement reads as its body loads is answered.
A name is answered once however often the statement reads it.
A declaration that runs nothing as the body loads reads nothing.
A name the statement itself binds is not read from outside the body.
A statement above is answered for a variable statement alone.
A name a function holds is read where that function is called rather than as the body loads.
A name a type holds is read by nothing.
A key a value spells bare is no name read.
A name read as the body loads that the body binds nowhere comes from outside the body.
The name answered is the first name read that way.
The statement answered is the first one above that declaration that runs.
The statement is answered as its first line rather than whole.
Which names a body binds is read from `name-binding` rather than here.
Nothing here says what a caller does with what is answered.

definition: the names a statement reads from outside its body as it loads, and what runs above a declaration
